evidence_of_benefit: Reference condition. Project simulation with real recorded tremor: at the mild class the ordinary pen reads as well as no tremor; moderate 5.7 of 10 words; severe 0.5 of 10 (SIM, docs/claims_register.md)
weaknesses: Illegible at severe tremor; no help with size (micrographia)
relevance_to_our_options: Anchor condition in EXP-U06/U07

mechanism: added mass and a thicker grip
regulatory_status: consumer product (a US daily activity assist device would be Class I, 510(k)-exempt: PDT-114)
evidence_of_benefit: PD pilot (n = 8): weighted pen increased the variability of the distance between letter peaks (PDT-21). ET: no published trial of weighted utensils (PDT-111). Spoons: users rated a weighted spoon as highly as Liftware (ACT-18, PDT-24) and preferred it in ET (ACT-19)
evidence_strength: weak (pilots, preference studies; none on ET writing)
weaknesses: Fatigue from weight; may worsen PD writing; no size help
relevance_to_our_options: The cheapest credible comparator: every pen option must beat it on a pre-registered margin

product_or_approach: Large or ergonomic grip pen (e.g. Parkinson's UK light-touch pen)
evidence_of_benefit: None found (GAP)
relevance_to_our_options: Comparator for grip-related comfort; charity shop is a sales channel

mechanism: magnetic pen and clipboard; weighted core; wide triangular grip
writing_jobs_served: paper on the supplied clipboard (desk tasks)
evidence_of_benefit: Developer reports feedback from more than 40 people; no controlled data (PDT-26); its micrographia claim conflicts with PDT-21
weaknesses: Clipboard needed; mass may hurt PD fluency; no evidence
relevance_to_our_options: Closest existing 'pen system'; also a desk-surface competitor

product_or_approach: Lined paper, visual cues and home writing practice (PD micrographia)
evidence_of_benefit: Parallel lines: word length 23.36 vs 17.83 cm (n = 11, PDT-33); 1.0 cm cues improved size (PDT-18); intensive amplitude training improved size by 7-17 % with retention but cost fluency (PDT-16, PDT-17); self-managed home programme improved amplitude (d = 0.80-1.07, PDT-20)
weaknesses: Needs practice and adherence; effects modest
relevance_to_our_options: The therapy tool and tablet app must beat paper cues and practice alone

mechanism: battery-free damping glove (tuned mass damper / magnetic stabilisation per manufacturer)
evidence_of_benefit: Manufacturer: 84 % improved vs no device, 70 % vs placebo glove (blinded neurologists); no peer-reviewed trial found; none for the earlier Steadi-Two (PDT-111)
weaknesses: Price; bulk; one hand per unit; unverified evidence
relevance_to_our_options: Mid-price anchor; 30-day money-back model

regulatory_status: needs a physician order; possibly insurance-covered (review)
evidence_of_benefit: No published clinical data (PDT-111)
relevance_to_our_options: Shows a prescription route for a passive aid

mechanism: spinning gyroscope on the back of the hand
regulatory_status: not registered with the MHRA (manufacturer disclaimer)
evidence_of_benefit: Manufacturer pilot abstract, n = 15 ET: ADL writing -48 % vs no device, -40 % vs placebo (p < 0.01 / p < 0.1) (ACT-25); multicentre trial results not reported (PDT-111)
relevance_to_our_options: Upper price anchor; the only active device with a writing outcome

mechanism: motors move the utensil against tremor
evidence_of_benefit: Pilot, 15 ET: 71-76 % accelerometer tremor reduction; 2 severe cases could not use it (ACT-16); rated no better than a weighted spoon (ACT-18)
weaknesses: Eating only; saturates with severe tremor; availability uncertain (site unavailable 2026-09-30)
relevance_to_our_options: The active-handheld precedent: modest price, preference parity with a weighted utensil

evidence_of_benefit: ET eating task (n = 20): successful transfer 88.9 % vs weighted 80.7 % and control 74.3 %; preference rank weighted 2.40 vs Gyenno 3.80 (ACT-19)
relevance_to_our_options: Evidence that preference can favour passive aids even when active ones perform

mechanism: wrist-worn peripheral nerve stimulation in repeated sessions
regulatory_status: prescription; US Medicare coverage under LCD L39591 (E0734)
evidence_of_benefit: Open-label home study, 263 ET: 68 % of moderate/severe improved to mild/slight on Bain-Findley ADL; 18 % device-related AEs (PDT-112)
evidence_strength: moderate (large open-label; earlier sham-controlled studies not opened)
weaknesses: Benefit wanes after stimulation; prescription; skin irritation; one arm
relevance_to_our_options: Shows the payer route: writing ADL items as coverage criteria (PDT-113)

mechanism: captures ink digitally on dot paper; no stabilisation
evidence_of_benefit: Learning disability meta-analysis: smart pens g = 0.449 (4 small publications) (HAP-50); none in tremor
relevance_to_our_options: Capture is a commodity; do not sell on capture

product_or_approach: Tablet with stylus (e.g. iPad + Apple Pencil) and handwriting apps
mechanism: digital ink on glass; apps for practice or measurement
writing_jobs_served: digital notes, drawing, practice, measurement; not paper
price_basis: iPad from 449 (UK from GBP 429) plus Apple Pencil (USB-C) 79 (Pro 129)
regulatory_status: consumer product; an app with medical claims could be software as a medical device (PDT-114)
evidence_of_benefit: Tablet measurement of dysgraphia: sensitivity 96.6 %, specificity 99.2 % (HAP-157); no evidence found of tremor-writing benefit
weaknesses: Not paper; glass is slippery; needs a device
relevance_to_our_options: Platform for the tablet-app and therapy options; competitor for digital note-taking

product_or_approach: Phone/tablet keyboard with touch accessibility settings (Hold Duration, Ignore Repeat, Tap Assistance)
writing_jobs_served: any text that may be typed
price_basis: with a device the person owns
evidence_of_benefit: None found for these settings (GAP). Typing or mouse use affected in 54 % of IETF respondents (PDT-99) and phone typing in 50 % of 20 ET (PDT-100); keyboard 52 WPM in healthy adults (HAP-161)
weaknesses: Tremor also affects typing; setup knowledge needed
relevance_to_our_options: Mandatory comparator (DEC-092); free

evidence_of_benefit: Not reviewed (GAP)
relevance_to_our_options: Comparator for desk tasks

writing_jobs_served: any text that may be dictated
evidence_of_benefit: Typical speakers: 153 vs 52 WPM keyboard (HAP-161). PD speech: research baseline recogniser 36.3 % word errors vs 3.4 % typical (PDT-104); voice problems in about 90 % of PD (PDT-103)
evidence_strength: strong for typical speakers; weak for PD
weaknesses: Soft or unclear speech; noise; privacy; cannot sign or fill paper
relevance_to_our_options: Mandatory comparator; likely better than any pen for long text if speech is clear

mechanism: speech recognition personalised for non-standard speech
evidence_of_benefit: Not reviewed (GAP); vendor says most effective for mild to moderate impairment
relevance_to_our_options: Assistive software sells as a subscription (price anchor)

evidence_of_benefit: Not reviewed
relevance_to_our_options: Not an available alternative today

product_or_approach: PD remote-monitoring wearables (PKG, Kinesia 360, KinesiaU, PDMonitor, STAT-ON)
maker_or_provider: Global Kinetics; Great Lakes NeuroTechnologies; PD Neurotechnology; Sense4care
price: 225 per use (PKG); 64 per patient-month (KinesiaU); 224 per month (Kinesia 360); 12000 or 350 per month (PDMonitor); 1600 per year (STAT-ON)
evidence_of_benefit: Conditionally recommended by NICE pending evidence on impact and resource use (PDT-115)
evidence_strength: moderate for measurement; uncertain for outcomes
relevance_to_our_options: Budget competitor and price anchor for the measuring pen

regulatory_status: CE marking reported in company statements (not verified)
evidence_of_benefit: Accuracy figures only in unverified summaries (HAP-166)
relevance_to_our_options: Direct precedent for the measuring pen

product_or_approach: Digitising tablet assessment of handwriting (research tools)
mechanism: tablet with paper overlay; kinematic features
evidence_of_benefit: Dysgraphia classification 96.6 % / 99.2 % (HAP-157); ET tablet tremor MDC 51 % (PDT-12)
relevance_to_our_options: Low-cost route to a measuring product

evidence_of_benefit: Effective programmes include at least 20 practice sessions; kinesthetic training alone did not help (HAP-41, HAP-42)
relevance_to_our_options: The therapy tool must fit inside these programmes, not replace practice

product_or_approach: Tremor medication, deep brain stimulation, focused ultrasound
evidence_of_benefit: 74 % of diagnosed US ET received possible treatment (PDT-96); in an IETF survey 33 % had no benefit from beta-blockers and 35 % stopped for side effects (PDT-99)
relevance_to_our_options: Reduces or changes the need; users on treatment are the likeliest pen users
